# Inter-agent handoffs in futon3c

This file is a coordination scratchpad for agents working on futon3c at the
same time. New entries go at the top; resolved entries can be moved to a
historical-notes section or removed once their hand-off is complete.

## Open hand-offs

### 2026-06-11 — M-typed-bells protocol available behind flag

`FUTON3C_TYPED_BELLS` adds semantic bell fields without changing the default
bell path. With the flag off, `type`/`ref` payload fields are ignored. With the
flag on:

- `type=query` with no `ref` creates an ArSE question at send-time and stamps
  the new ArSE thread id into the invoke job's `ref`.
- `type=query --ref <ask-id>` routes an existing ArSE thread to another agent.
- `type=answer --ref <ask-id>` records an ArSE answer; `answer` without `ref`
  is rejected.
- Valid types: `query`, `answer`, `assert`, `challenge`, `agree`, `define`,
  `retract`, `suggest`, `request`.

Use `scripts/agency_send.py --type ... --ref ...` rather than hand-writing JSON.
The recipient prompt includes a `Type:` header when the flag is on.

### 2026-04-22 — `claude-15` → `claude-16` (Web War Machine)

**New endpoint available for the Web War Machine to consume.**

`GET /api/alpha/aif-stack/live` — the live-projected AIF+ self-model of
the futon stack. Same JVM, same port, same routing pattern as your
existing `/api/alpha/war-machine` handler.

- **Backend:** `futon3c/src/futon3c/aif/stack_generator.clj` — loads the
  cached structural prior at `futon5a/holes/stories/THE-STACK.aif.edn`
  (and the 16 leaf `.aif.edn` files alongside it), then overlays live
  mission status from `mcb/build-inventory`. Spine nodes whose `:origin`
  resolves to a `mission@repo` ref get a live-status overlay; others
  retain their cached status (those are sorry refs — v2 will query the
  sorry registry too).
- **Handler:** `handle-aif-stack-live` in `futon3c.transport.http` (right
  next to your `handle-war-machine`, same `requiring-resolve` shape).
- **JSON shape:** mirrors the EDN at
  `futon5a/holes/stories/THE-STACK.aif.edn` (you can read the .edn
  directly to see what to expect). Top-level keys include `:stack-spine`
  (10 nodes), `:stack-nodes` (the 10 spine entries with content/status/
  role/origin/cited-by), `:stack-conflicts` (4 coalesced from 16 leaf-
  level conflicts, with weights), `:stack-frames` (3 organising
  preferences), `:reading` (the human-readable next-move + level-0
  paragraph), plus liveness metadata: `:live?` `:live-mission-count`
  `:generated-at` `:live-data-source`.
- **Per-node liveness marker:** spine nodes carry `:live-status?` `true`
  when their status was overlaid from the live registry (currently S5
  and S6); cached-only nodes omit the marker.
- **Verified working:** the route is wired and the running server picked
  it up on 2026-04-22 at ~17:30Z (hot-swap via Drawbridge; no JVM
  restart). `curl http://localhost:7070/api/alpha/aif-stack/live`
  returns ~21 KB of JSON.

**Architectural framing for the client side.** The AIF+ stack data is
structurally a futon2-shaped belief state, but for the futon stack
itself rather than for ant agents. Joe's framing: "the War Machine is
the AIF ants viz-inspector for the stack." Three plausible client view
modes once you reach the right point in the visualiser work:

1. **Spine + conflict force-graph.** 10 spine nodes as larger circles
   colour-coded by status (green = settled/operational, amber =
   in-progress/active, grey = spec-only, prototype = striped); 4
   conflict nodes as red diamonds with attack arrows to the spine nodes
   they bite (`:bites` array). Stack frames (`:stack-frames`) as a
   tinted backdrop band over the substrate they `:over`.
2. **Drift glow** on stale leaves. The drift detector at
   `futon5a/scripts/detect_drift.clj --json` reports per-leaf staleness;
   render flicker on stale leaves the same way the War Machine pulses
   busy ants.
3. **Click-through inspector.** Click a spine node → side panel shows
   the leaves citing it (`:cited-by`), the conflicts biting it, the
   prose summary at `futon5a/holes/stories/<leaf>.aif.md`. Click a
   conflict → shows the leaf-level instances it coalesces from
   (`:coalesces-from` map).

I'm happy to coordinate on the rendering shape if it would help — drop
a note here or just send a message to me (claude-15) via Joe.

**Why this matters for War Machine.** It turns the visualiser from
"futon0's strategic UI" into "the stack's AIF ant viewer." Same
visualiser, additional view-mode that switches between the strategic
hex map and the AIF+ self-model graph.

**Cached-vs-live discipline (reference for v2 work).** The `.aif.edn`
files are the structural prior (which 10 nodes form the spine, what the

registry supplies the data layer (statuses, counts). Periodic LLM
re-derivation refreshes the structural prior when enough has shifted.
The drift detector at `futon5a/scripts/detect_drift.clj` is the
interoception readout for both layers; it now feeds the Stack HUD via
`futon0/contrib/stack-hud-self-description.el`.

{"content":"# C1 INITIAL — zai-student-transfer-20260910

## Pattern use (search: see c1-initial-tools.txt)

- **Retrieved:** 5 patterns (ids above). **Actually read (2):**
  - `math-formalization-CA/uniform-continuity-boundedness` @ `a24aa6c9…7272c` — "bound the image before/instead of mixing modulus and magnitude; boundedness of the image is where the domain's boundedness enters."
  - `math-informal/local-to-global` @ `ac568c2e…fb63` — "cover with pieces where the property is manageable, prove on each, assemble globally; here no overlap-compatibility condition is needed, just max over centers."
- Claimed used = proof-supported used = exactly these two. Not read: metric-cauchy-convergence, estimate-by-bounding, unfold-the-definition (titles only). No memory store consulted.

## Premises

Required:
1. X nonempty, totally bounded — **given**.
2. Y normed real vector space (only vector-space/norm facts used: triangle inequality, ||·|| homogeneity-free lower bound 0) — **given**.
3. F nonempty, **uniformly equicontinuous**: ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 ∀f∈F ∀x,y: d(x,y)<δ ⇒ ‖f(x)−f(y)‖<ε — **given**.
4. Pointwise bounded: ∀x ∃B_x<∞ ∀f: ‖f(x)‖≤B_x — **given**.

Not needed / absent: completeness of X, compactness (total boundedness alone suffices — no sequential argument), any structure on Y beyond the norm. Unchecked: nothing external; the proof is self-contained elementary estimates.

## Theorem

∃M<∞ such that ‖f(x)‖ ≤ M for all f∈F, x∈X. (Equivalently: the family F is uniformly bounded.)

## Proof

Fix ε = 1. By uniform equicontinuity there is δ > 0 such that

  (★) for all f∈F and all x,y∈X with d(x,y) < δ:  ‖f(x) − f(y)‖ < 1.

**Step 1 (finite net).** Since X is totally bounded, the open cover {B(x,δ) : x∈X} admits a finite subcover: there exist x₁,…,x_n ∈ X with X = ⋃_{i=1}^n B(x_i, δ). This is where the domain hypothesis enters — exactly the entry point flagged by `uniform-continuity-boundedness` ("the step between [continuity and boundedness] is exactly where the domain's boundedness enters").

**Step 2 (bound on the net).** By pointwise boundedness, for each i choose finite B_i with ‖f(x_i)‖ ≤ B_i for all f∈F. Set

  M := max_{1≤i≤n} B_i + 1.

M is finite (max of finitely many finite numbers, plus 1).

**Step 3 (local-to-global patch).** Let f∈F and x∈X be arbitrary. By Step 1 there is i with d(x, x_i) < δ. Then, by the triangle inequality in Y and (★),

  ‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f(x) − f(x_i)‖ + ‖f(x_i)‖ < 1 + B_i ≤ 1 + M′ ≤ M,

where M′ := max_i B_i, so M = M′ + 1. Since f and x were arbitrary, M bounds ‖f(x)‖ over all of F × X. ∎

Note on patching (per `local-to-global`'s HOWEVER clause): here the local bounds need no compatibility on overlaps — each x is assigned to *some* net point, and the same uniform δ works everywhere; the assembly is a max, not a gluing, so no overlap check is required. That clause was deliberately discharged rather than ignored.

## Does "each f uniformly continuous" suffice?

**No.** Uniform equicontinuity is strictly stronger: it requires one δ to serve all f∈F simultaneously, whereas "each f uniformly continuous" permits δ = δ(f, ε) depending on f.

**Counterexample.** Take X = {0} ⊂ ℝ (nonempty, totally bounded), Y = ℝ, and F = {f_n : n ∈ ℕ} with f_n(0) = n. Every f_n is (trivially) uniformly continuous — on a one-point space *every* map is uniformly continuous. But F is not even pointwise bounded at 0 (B_0 would have to dominate every n), so pointwise boundedness already fails, and a fortiori no finite M exists: ‖f_n(0)‖ = n → ∞.

If one wants a counterexample preserving pointwise boundedness but failing the conclusion, that is impossible on totally bounded X — that is exactly the theorem just proved — so pointwise-bounded failure must use a non-totally-bounded domain; but the question as posed ("does the weaker per-f hypothesis suffice to derive the conclusion?") is answered negatively by the example above, where all per-f uniform continuity holds and the conclusion is false. (Uniform equicontinuity also fails there, for ε=1 no single δ consideration can help since boundedness fails outright — consistent with the pattern's observation that the modulus says nothing about the *size* of values.)

## Difficulty / limitations

- **Difficulty observed:** none of substance. The 1-net + triangle-inequality estimate is the standard proof of the "uniformly bounded" half of Arzelà–Ascoli-type results; total boundedness replaces compactness cleanly because no limit extraction is needed. My main hesitation was checking that no completeness/compactness is smuggled in — it is not: Steps 1–3 use only total boundedness, equicontinuity, pointwise boundedness, and the norm axioms.
- Limitation: the bound M produced is non-constructive only in choosing which finite subcover/net to use (fine, X arbitrary metric); each B_x is assumed given, not computed.
- The equicontinuity point of the counterexample: on a one-point space even equicontinuity holds, so the counterexample in fact shows pointwise boundedness is indispensable, while the theorem shows it is sufficient *with* equicontinuity. If the intended counterexample to "each f uniformly continuous suffices" must keep pointwise boundedness and total boundedness, no such example can exist by the theorem; hence any legitimate counterexample must drop one of the other hypotheses, and dropping total boundedness works: X = ℤ ⊂ ℝ, Y = ℝ, f_n(k) = n·|sin(π k /n)|-free simpler: f_n(k) = min(n,|k|) — each uniformly continuous, ‖f_n(0)‖=0 bounded pointwise... but X not totally bounded, outside the stated hypotheses. I state this honestly as the boundary of what the weaker hypothesis gives.
